logic_node.action: Consider ICD despite uncertain mortality benefit in nonischemic DCM
logic_node.action_detail: In the DANISH trial, patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and LVEF <=35% randomized to ICD showed no reduction in total mortality but did show a reduction in sudden cardiac death risk. 58% of patients received CRT, possibly mitigating ICD benefit. The mortality benefit of ICD in nonischemic DCM remains less certain than in ischemic cardiomyopathy.

source_text: In the DANISH trial, patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy and LVEF <= 35% randomized to ICD showed no reduction in total mortality, but there was a reduction in SCD risk. 58% of patients received CRT, possibly mitigating ICD benefit.

logic_node.action: Prioritize CRT in LBBB with QRS >=150 ms for highest value
logic_node.action_detail: CRT provides highest economic value and greatest clinical benefit in patients with LBBB and QRS duration >=150 ms. Cost per QALY is <$60,000 in this population. Wider QRS durations and LBBB morphology are the strongest predictors of CRT response across COMPANION, CARE-HF, MADIT-CRT, REVERSE, and RAFT trials.

source_text: The most benefit was gained with wider QRS durations and with LBBB...cost per QALY is <$60,000. Among populations with larger expected mortality reduction, such as patients with LBBB with QRS duration >150 ms.

logic_node.action: Implant ICD for LMNA/C cardiomyopathy even with LVEF >35%
logic_node.action_detail: Specific arrhythmogenic genetic variants such as LMNA/C, desmosomal proteins, phospholamban, and Filamin-C carry implications for ICD implantation for primary prevention of sudden death even in patients with LVEF >35% or <3 months of GDMT. Most patients with LMNA/C cardiomyopathy will progress to cardiac transplantation, sometimes precipitated by refractory arrhythmias more than by pump failure.

source_text: LMNA/C, desmosomal proteins, phospholamban, and Filamin-C carry implications for ICD implantation for primary prevention of sudden death even in patients who have LVEF >35%, or <3 months of GDMT.

logic_node.action: Prefer CRT over RV pacing in AV block with LVEF <=50%
logic_node.action_detail: In the BLOCK-HF trial, patients with NYHA class I-III HF, LVEF <=50%, and atrioventricular block randomized to CRT versus RV pacing showed benefit from CRT in reduction of death, urgent HF visit, or 15% increase in LV end-systolic volume. CRT should be preferred over RV pacing when ventricular pacing is required in this population.

source_text: In the BLOCK-HF trial, patients with NYHA class I to III HF, LVEF <= 50%, and atrioventricular block randomized to RV pacing or CRT, there was benefit to CRT in reduction in death, urgent HF visit, or 15% increase in LV end systolic volume.

logic_node.action: Do not implant CRT for narrow QRS despite mechanical dyssynchrony
logic_node.action_detail: Extension of CRT benefit to patients with narrow QRS has generally failed. RETHINQ (QRS <130 ms), ECHO-CRT (QRS <=130 ms with mechanical dyssynchrony on echo), and LESSER-EARTH (QRS <120 ms) trials all showed no benefit from CRT. Echocardiographic dyssynchrony does not predict CRT response in narrow QRS patients.

source_text: Extension of benefit to patients with narrow QRS has been attempted but has generally failed. In RETHINQ, ECHO-CRT, and LESSER-EARTH trials there was no benefit from CRT in patients with QRS <130 ms.

logic_node.action: Optimize GDMT before ICD or CRT implantation
logic_node.action_detail: GDMT should be optimized before ICD and CRT implantation to assess whether LVEF improves sufficiently to no longer meet device criteria. The seminal RCTs for ICDs and CRTs enrolled patients on background medical therapy.

source_text: GDMT is optimized before ICD and CRT implantation to assess whether the LVEF improves.

logic_node.action: Consider baroreflex activation therapy when unsuited for CRT
logic_node.action_detail: In a prospective multicenter RCT of 408 patients with NYHA class III HF and LVEF <=35%, baroreceptor stimulation was associated with improvements in QOL, exercise capacity, and NT-proBNP levels. No mortality or hospitalization benefit has been demonstrated. Approved for patients unsuited for other HF devices including CRT.

source_text: In a prospective, multicenter, RCT with 408 patients with NYHA class III HF, LVEF <= 35%, baroreceptor stimulation was associated with improvements in QOL, exercise capacity, and NT-proBNP levels.

logic_node.action: Consider cardiac contractility modulation when CRT not appropriate
logic_node.action_detail: Cardiac contractility modulation (CCM) applies high-voltage, long-duration electric signals to the RV septal wall during the absolute myocardial refractory period, augmenting LV contractile performance. FDA-approved for NYHA class III with LVEF 25-45% who are not candidates for CRT. Four RCTs showed benefits in exercise capacity and QOL but no mortality or hospitalization benefit.

source_text: CCM is FDA-approved for patients with NYHA class III with LVEF of 25% to 45% who are not candidates for CRT. Four RCTs have shown benefits in exercise capacity and QOL but no benefits in death or hospitalizations.

logic_node.action: Do not use vagus nerve stimulation for HFrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Although early trials of vagus nerve stimulation were positive, the largest and latest trial (INOVATE-HF) did not show a reduction in mortality and HF hospitalizations. Vagus nerve stimulation is not recommended for HFrEF.

source_text: Although early trials of vagus nerve stimulation were positive, the largest and latest trial did not show a reduction in mortality and HF hospitalizations.

logic_node.action: Perform CABG plus GDMT for ischemic cardiomyopathy
logic_node.action_detail: CABG plus GDMT did not reduce all-cause mortality at median 56 months but at 10-year follow-up showed significant reductions in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and death from any cause or cardiovascular hospitalization in patients with LVEF <=35% and ischemic cardiomyopathy. Long-term survival benefit is greater with lower EF or 3-vessel disease and diminishes with increasing age.

source_text: At 10 years follow-up, CABG+GDMT resulted in significant reductions in all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, and death or cardiovascular hospitalization in patients with LVEF <= 35% and ischemic cardiomyopathy.

conditions.threshold: left main or left main equivalent

logic_node.action: Perform CABG for left main or left main equivalent disease with HF
logic_node.action_detail: CABG has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with left main or left main equivalent coronary artery disease and HF. Long-term follow-up shows reduction in all-cause, cardiovascular, and HF hospitalizations and in all-cause and cardiovascular mortality compared with GDMT alone.

source_text: CABG has been shown to improve outcomes in patients with left main or left main equivalent disease and HF. Long-term follow-up shows a reduction in all-cause, cardiovascular, and HF hospitalizations and in all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.

logic_node.action: Do not routinely add surgical ventricular reconstruction to CABG
logic_node.action_detail: An RCT of CABG combined with surgical ventricular remodeling compared with CABG alone did not show reduction in death or hospitalization, or improvement in symptoms. Surgical ventricular remodeling at time of CABG may be useful only in patients with intractable HF, large thrombus, or persistent arrhythmias from well-defined aneurysm or scar, if other therapies are ineffective or contraindicated.

source_text: An RCT of CABG combined with surgical ventricular remodeling compared with CABG alone did not show a reduction in death or hospitalization, or improvement in symptoms with surgical ventricular remodeling.

logic_node.action: Perform AV nodal ablation to ensure near 100% CRT pacing in AF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with AF undergoing CRT, atrioventricular node ablation or pharmacological rate control should ensure near 100% ventricular pacing. In the PAVE study, patients with AF undergoing AV node ablation showed improved 6-minute walk test and LVEF with CRT compared with RV pacing. Benefits of CRT in AF were shown in MUSTIC AF, RAFT, and SPARE trials, while AF attenuated CRT benefit in COMPANION.

source_text: In PAVE, patients with AF undergoing AV node ablation, CRT improved the 6-minute walk test and LVEF compared with RV pacing. Benefits in MUSTIC AF, RAFT, and SPARE; AF attenuated CRT benefit in COMPANION.

logic_node.action: Assess arrhythmic vs nonarrhythmic death risk for ICD value
logic_node.action_detail: A transvenous ICD provides high economic value in primary prevention of SCD particularly when the patient's risk of death from ventricular arrhythmia is deemed high and the risk of nonarrhythmic death (cardiac or noncardiac) is deemed low based on comorbidities and functional status. ICD does not provide value when survival is not increased, as shown in the CABG Patch trial.

source_text: A transvenous ICD provides high economic value in primary prevention of SCD particularly when the patient's risk of death caused by ventricular arrhythmia is deemed high and the risk of nonarrhythmic death is deemed low.
